description: The classic data structures and algorithm design techniques, each analysed for correctness and running time and implemented in C++ with tests. Taught to the depth of a leading algorithms course.
modelledOn: Cormen, Leiserson, Rivest and Stein, Introduction to Algorithms
Weiss, Data Structures and Algorithm Analysis in C++
outcomes: Specify abstract data types and implement them in C++ with clear interfaces, invariants and tests.
Analyse the time and space complexity of iterative and recursive algorithms, including amortised analysis.
Implement and choose among lists, stacks, queues, hash tables, balanced trees, heaps and graphs.
Implement and compare sorting and searching algorithms and justify their bounds.
Apply greedy, divide-and-conquer, dynamic programming, randomised and backtracking techniques to new problems.
Solve graph problems with BFS, DFS, shortest paths, minimum spanning trees and topological sort.

units.title: Data structures, abstract data types and analysis of algorithms
topics: Abstract data types versus implementations; interfaces, invariants and encapsulation in C++ classes and templates
Models of computation; counting operations; best, worst and average case
Asymptotic notation: O, Omega, Theta; growth rates and limits
Analysing loops and nested loops; recurrences and the master theorem
Amortised analysis: dynamic arrays and the aggregate and accounting methods
Measuring running time experimentally and comparing with theory

units.title: Lists, stacks and queues
topics: Array lists and dynamic resizing; singly, doubly and circular linked lists; iterators
Stacks: array and linked implementations; expression evaluation, balanced brackets, undo
Queues and deques; circular buffers; priority queue as an ADT
The C++ STL: vector, list, deque, stack, queue and their complexity guarantees

units.title: Recursion
topics: Recursive thinking and the call stack; base cases and progress
Recursion versus iteration; tail recursion; memoisation
Classic problems: permutations, subsets, Tower of Hanoi, flood fill, binary search
Proving recursive algorithms correct by induction

units.title: Sorting
topics: Insertion, selection and bubble sort; stability and in-place sorting
Merge sort and quicksort: analysis, pivot choice, randomised quicksort
Heaps and heapsort; the binary heap as a priority queue
Lower bound for comparison sorting; counting sort, radix sort, bucket sort
Choosing a sort: std::sort, introsort and when each algorithm wins

units.title: Searching and hashing
topics: Linear and binary search; interpolation search; order statistics and quickselect
Hash functions, uniform hashing, universal hashing
Collision resolution: chaining, open addressing (linear, quadratic, double hashing); load factor and rehashing
Hash tables in practice: unordered_map, string hashing, Bloom filters
Applications: dictionaries, counting, deduplication, caching

units.title: Trees
topics: Tree terminology; binary trees and traversals (preorder, inorder, postorder, level order)
Binary search trees: search, insert, delete; expected height
Balanced trees: AVL rotations; red-black trees; 2-3 trees and B-trees for disks
Tries and suffix trees for strings; Huffman coding trees
Augmented trees: order statistics, interval trees; segment trees and Fenwick trees
std::map and std::set and their guarantees

units.title: Graphs
topics: Graph representations: adjacency matrix and list; weighted and directed graphs
Breadth-first and depth-first search; connected components; cycle detection
Topological sort and DAGs; strongly connected components
Shortest paths: Dijkstra with a heap, Bellman-Ford, Floyd-Warshall; the tro-tro route problem
Minimum spanning trees: Kruskal with union-find, Prim
Network flow in brief: Ford-Fulkerson and bipartite matching

units.title: Design techniques
topics: Greedy: activity selection, fractional knapsack, Huffman, interval scheduling; proving greedy choices
Divide-and-conquer: closest pair, Karatsuba multiplication, Strassen in brief
Dynamic programming: 0/1 knapsack, longest common subsequence, edit distance, matrix chain, coin change in cedis
Randomised algorithms: randomised quicksort, hashing, Monte Carlo and Las Vegas
Backtracking and branch-and-bound: N-queens, sudoku, subset sum
Introduction to NP-completeness and what to do when no fast algorithm is known

schedule.title: ADTs and asymptotic analysis
schedule.exercise: Problem set: rank twelve functions by growth rate, prove two Big-O claims from the definition, and write the interface and invariants of a Stack ADT before any implementation.

tasks.title: Plot n, n log n, n squared and 2 to the n for n up to 30 and order the four growth rates
Implement a templated C++ Stack class with a documented interface and invariant, and verify it with ten push and pop tests
Count the primitive operations of three given functions in best, worst and average case, then confirm the counts by instrumenting the code on random inputs

schedule.title: Analysing loops, recurrences and amortised cost
schedule.exercise: Solve five recurrences with the master theorem, and justify by the accounting method why appending to a doubling array costs constant amortised time.

tasks.title: Step through a nested loop in the visualiser, count executions of the inner statement for n = 8, and match the result to the formula
Run 33 appends on a doubling dynamic array, track each resize and copy, and compute the amortised cost per append
Time insertion sort and merge sort on random inputs from 1000 to 64000 elements, fit growth curves, and compare them with the predicted complexities

schedule.title: Lists, stacks and queues
schedule.exercise: Coding kata: implement a circular-buffer queue and use a stack to evaluate postfix expressions, with five tests each including empty and full edge cases.

tasks.title: Insert and delete nodes in a singly linked list in the visualiser, tracing pointer changes for the head, middle and tail
Use a stack to check balanced brackets and evaluate postfix expressions in C++, with tests on ten valid and invalid strings
Implement a circular-buffer queue and a deque, then benchmark them against std::list and std::vector for one million operations

schedule.title: Recursion and proof of correctness
schedule.exercise: Prove by induction that a recursive binary search is correct, and write the recurrence for the number of calls made by recursive Fibonacci.

tasks.title: Step through recursive factorial of 5 and watch the call stack grow and unwind, noting each frame's argument and return value
Convert recursive Fibonacci to a memoised and an iterative version, and compare the number of calls and runtime for n = 35
Write recursive solutions for generating all permutations, all subsets and Tower of Hanoi, and verify the counts for n up to 10

schedule.title: Elementary and divide-and-conquer sorting
schedule.exercise: Hand-trace insertion sort, merge sort and quicksort on the same eight values, and say which sorts are stable and in place.

tasks.title: Step through insertion sort on eight values and record the comparisons and shifts made at each pass
Run quicksort on sorted, reversed and random arrays with first-element and median-of-three pivots, and compare the comparison counts
Implement heapsort with a binary heap from scratch, verify it on 1000 random arrays against the library sort, and count comparisons

schedule.title: Sorting lower bounds and choosing a sort
schedule.exercise: Short essay: pick the best sort for four data sets (nearly sorted, huge integers, small range, records needing stability) and justify each choice.

tasks.title: Run counting sort on twenty small integers, show the count array and output placement, and explain why it is stable
Implement radix sort for 6-digit student ID numbers and compare its running time with std::sort on 100000 numbers
Benchmark five sorts on sorted, reversed, random and many-duplicate inputs, then write a rule for choosing among them with measured evidence

schedule.title: Searching and hash tables
schedule.exercise: Problem set: insert a given key sequence into hash tables with chaining and linear probing, compute load factors, and count probes for successful and failed searches.

tasks.title: Run binary search on a sorted array of 31 values and count the comparisons for three keys, including one not present
Insert twelve keys into a hash table using chaining, linear probing and double hashing, and compare the number of probes of each
Build an open-addressing hash table with rehashing and measure how lookup time grows as load factor approaches 0.9, then add a Bloom filter in front

schedule.title: Trees, BSTs and balanced trees
schedule.exercise: Draw the trees after inserting a given sequence into a BST, an AVL tree and a 2-3 tree, and compare their heights.

tasks.title: Build a binary tree from eleven values and list its preorder, inorder, postorder and level-order traversals
Insert and delete keys in a binary search tree, including a node with two children, and trace the resulting structure
Insert 20 ascending keys into a plain BST and an AVL tree, record every rotation, and compare tree heights and search costs

schedule.title: Tries, augmented trees and ordered containers
schedule.exercise: Design a phone-directory structure for a mobile money agent app, choosing between a trie, a std::map and a hash table and justifying the choice.

tasks.title: Insert eight words into a trie and trace the search for a prefix and for a word that is absent
Build the Huffman tree for a given character frequency table, derive the codes, and compute the compression ratio
Implement a Fenwick tree for prefix sums, check it against a brute-force version on random updates, and compare query times for 100000 elements

schedule.title: Graph representations and traversals
schedule.exercise: Model a small tro-tro route network as a graph, run BFS and DFS by hand from a chosen start, and give the topological order of a course-prerequisite DAG.

tasks.title: Convert a seven-node weighted directed graph between adjacency matrix and adjacency list forms, and compare their memory use
Run BFS and DFS from the same start on a ten-node graph, list visit orders, and find all connected components
Implement topological sort and Tarjan's strongly connected components, and test them on a prerequisite graph containing one deliberate cycle

schedule.title: Shortest paths, spanning trees and flow
schedule.exercise: Solve a shortest-path and a minimum-spanning-tree problem on the same road network with a weighted edge list, and explain why the two answers differ.

tasks.title: Run Dijkstra's algorithm from one node of a six-node weighted graph and record the distance table after each step
Build a minimum spanning tree of a ten-node cable network with Kruskal and union-find, then check it against Prim's tree
Find cheapest tro-tro routes between towns with Dijkstra, then add a negative-cost promotion edge and show where Dijkstra fails and Bellman-Ford succeeds

schedule.title: Greedy, divide-and-conquer and dynamic programming
schedule.exercise: For three problems decide whether greedy works, give a counter-example where it fails, and write the recurrence for the dynamic programming alternative.

tasks.title: Run greedy interval scheduling on nine activities and list the chosen set, then check no other schedule has more activities
Fill the dynamic programming table for 0/1 knapsack with six items and recover the chosen items by backtracking
Compute the fewest coins for a cedi amount with greedy and DP for a custom coin system, and find a system where greedy gives the wrong answer

schedule.title: Randomised, backtracking and hard problems
schedule.exercise: Short report: for N-queens and subset sum, describe the search tree, the pruning rule, and why subset sum is NP-complete but still solvable for small inputs.

tasks.title: Solve 4-queens by backtracking in the visualiser and note every placement that is abandoned and the reason
Compare deterministic and randomised quicksort on adversarial inputs over 100 runs, and report the mean and worst running time of each
Solve subset sum with plain backtracking and with branch-and-bound pruning, and compare nodes explored on 25 random instances
